findings.fix: Change 2,360 to 2,381 at L740 and in the knob row. Use 756 B at WM-3 and AC-WM-75 and drop 'about 700' and 'about 735'. The AC pass line (at most 2 KB) is fine.

findings.section: D.13 settle_lint, AC-WM-69, AC-WM-78, ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS
findings.finding: The 24-tick lower bound is sized from Layout's init-time BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME (256). Nothing shows that the PROJECTOR's scene build at arrival runs at that rate. AC-WM-78 ('completes within 2 frames') has no measurement behind it, and it is listed as BLOCKING Integration. The default 45 is a PLACEHOLDER, which is fine, but AC-WM-78 as written cannot be verified.
findings.fix: Rewrite AC-WM-78 as a spike gate: 'On RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, the PROJECTOR build of home+B (331 tiles) completes in <= ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS - ARRIVE_MARGIN_TICKS ticks at P99; the measured frame count replaces ceil(331/256) in D.13'. Mark it pending spike.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria gate table Performance row (L1746); AC-WM-77
findings.finding: After R12 the gate row still says 'the measuring machine recorded in the evidence file | ADVISORY'. AC-WM-77 itself names RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK and a '10 % P99 headroom under the 16.6 ms / 33.3 ms ceilings'. But its pass lines are STEP_BUDGET_MS 4 and 0.1 ms per tick, so how a P99 frame-time figure relates to them is undefined.
findings.fix: Update the row to 'RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK per qa.min_spec; pending spike; ADVISORY until measured'. In AC-WM-77 state the pass test as: the three applies <= 4 ms and transit.step <= 0.1 ms at P99 on both machines, and the frame P99 with the apply in it is <= 90 % of the ceiling.

findings.section: Untestable ACs (rewrites): AC-WM-29, AC-WM-37 gate (2), AC-WM-67(h)/G-2, AC-WM-26b, AC-WM-81d, Feel Acceptance Criteria
findings.finding: Several ACs still cannot be pass/failed by a tester. AC-WM-29 gates on 'art-director sign-off' with no checklist. AC-WM-37 gate (2) depends on a 'typical draw' that is undefined. AC-WM-67(h) LEG_FOUL has no clearance number or tool. AC-WM-26b is 'provisional on Attention confirming the intake slot', although Attention confirmed route 1 on 2026-10-28 (R20). findings.fix: AC-WM-29 -> 'screenshots retained show (i) plate fully black for >= 1 frame at each cut, (ii) running-light pool radius within +/-2 px of LEG_RUNNING_LIGHT_RADIUS_PX, (iii) warm point visible at both ladder extremes, (iv) dock cut is a single-frame cut'. AC-WM-37 (2) -> use the rated 2,500 W basis D.5 already fixes. AC-WM-67(h) -> 'swept pod path keeps >= N px (N tied to an existing constant) from every other footprint, evaluated by the named content tool'. findings.section: Whole document: amendment history interleaved with normative text (WM-8, WM-8b, WM-9, WM-26, WM-26b, D.15)

findings.finding: The AC-WM-129 title 'Hop-and-straight-back resets nothing' and E-60's 'meets a CALM derelict with the rearm timer set' overstate what happens. The tell IS voided (user ruling). findings.fix: Retitle AC-WM-129 'Hop-and-back heals nothing and voids the tell'. In E-60 say 'rearm_until_T was set at the due run (it may already have expired on return)'. Optionally add a degenerate-strategy note that hop-and-back is a 400 mL, about 31 s tell purge, which is the ruled escape.

findings.section: Registry hop_fuel comment (entities.yaml L5730); WM-8 first sentence; Tuning Knobs default leg speed row; WM-17 figures

findings.fix: Fix the registry comment to withdrawn_fuel_ml. Reword WM-8 to 'the only pick-driven write is pod_hop; berth and unberth are console presses with their own payloads'. findings.section: Open asks: ASK-PC-1, ASK-MSA-1, ASK-G1b, ASK-L1 (OQ-DA-17), AC-WM-133/134

findings.finding: Banner (6) says R13/R14 'need nothing here: this system stores and reads no restore_epoch'. That is wrong for the ACs. R13/R14 make that true only for a pinned (save, epoch) pair: a death restore or a kill-Continue advances the epoch, a QUIT-Continue carries it. No AC says the epoch is pinned. WEB_RESTORE_EPOCH (a stale leg_epoch) also collides in name with the kernel's restore_epoch.
findings.fix: Strike the banner dismissal. Add one clause to each listed AC: 'run with restore_epoch pinned to e in the restored and uninterrupted runs via request_restore(gen, e); threat draws are not compared across different epochs'. Rename WEB_RESTORE_EPOCH to WEB_RESTORE_LEG_EPOCH at L227, L871 and AC-WM-56 (L1613), and in the registry if it is listed.

They are BLOCKING and compare state_hash across every other block at T*+12, including attention.state, whose draws key on restore_epoch. They require two restored runs from one snapshot to be bit-identical and equal to the uninterrupted run. R13/R14 make that true only for a pinned (save, epoch) pair: a death restore or a kill-Continue advances the epoch, a QUIT-Continue carries it. No AC says the epoch is pinned. WEB_RESTORE_EPOCH (a stale leg_epoch) also collides in name with the kernel's restore_epoch.
